note2026_09_21_gate_needs_the_standard.task: With the Anthropic gate live, "네 말할수있습니다" was still written into the worksheet as a participant's example -- while the guide, in the same turn, correctly said it had not heard the situation yet.
note2026_09_21_gate_needs_the_standard.cause: Two model calls judge the same thing and only one had been told the standard. The dialogue agent gets the step's full task intent; the semantic gate got the generic system prompt, nodeGoal, and expectedAnswerDescription -- which was EMPTY, because it reads promptItem.modelGuidance || aiInstruction and neither was settable from a session spec. aiInstruction is the first line of the manual source range, which says nothing about what a valid answer is.
note2026_09_21_gate_needs_the_standard.sharedFileJustification: PromptSpec gains an optional modelGuidance and the compiler passes it through (source-fidelity-catalog.ts). Purely additive, no default behaviour change, and there was no session-local way to reach the gate at all -- which is the escalation test in .claude/rules/tbct-session-manual.md section 6.
note2026_09_21_gate_needs_the_standard.theStandard: Set on review-distortion: a valid answer is a concrete moment or the thought in it; a bare confirmation (네 / 네 있었어요 / 네 말할 수 있습니다 / yes I have) is clarification_request because the situation has not been given; having none for this pattern (딱히 없어요 / 떠오르지 않아요) is collection_stop.
note2026_09_21_gate_needs_the_standard.verifiedLive: The assessment route is open and takes a plain AssessmentRequest, so each phrasing can be checked against production directly with curl -- that is how the gap was found (네 있었어요 came back accept_answer with four other phrasings correct).

note2026_09_21_anthropic_assessment_prov.task: The semantic gate had no model behind it in production, so "네 있었어요" was still filed as a cognitive-distortion example after the gate was supposedly restored.
note2026_09_21_anthropic_assessment_prov.finding: ASSESSMENT_PROVIDER defaults to "deterministic" and the providers on offer were groq / ollama / gemini -- none of which is configured on the deployment, which carries ANTHROPIC_API_KEY only. So every answer was judged by DeterministicAssessmentModel: nonAnswer = an eleven-word English stop list, valid = !nonAnswer && length > 1. "네 이썼어요" passes both. Restoring the collection path (note2026_09_21_s02_model_judges_the_answer) moved the decision from my keyword list to a shared keyword list; it never reached a model. The dialogue agent was fine throughout -- it asked for the detail correctly -- because that is a different model call on a different key.
note2026_09_21_anthropic_assessment_prov.fix: AnthropicAssessmentModel in assessment-providers.ts, selected by ASSESSMENT_PROVIDER=anthropic, reading ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_MODEL.
note2026_09_21_anthropic_assessment_prov.whyAnthropicAndNotAKey: Chosen over configuring Groq or Gemini because the participant's sentence already goes to Anthropic on every turn to be phrased. No new recipient of patient text, no new credential, and nothing new for the study's ethics paperwork to cover.
note2026_09_21_anthropic_assessment_prov.structuredOutput: A forced tool call, like the dialogue agent. The Messages API has no JSON-schema response format, and parsing prose for JSON is how markup reached a participant once already (note2026_09_21_structured_output_leak). A truncated or unstructured reply throws rather than being read as an answer.
note2026_09_21_anthropic_assessment_prov.cloudSwitchRespected: allowCloudPatientAssessment is honoured, not waived, even though this vendor already sees the text -- it is a deliberate switch and not mine to weaken. That makes ALLOW_CLOUD_PATIENT_ASSESSMENT=true a second required variable; without it every walkthrough answer throws, and assessRuntimePatientInput fails CLOSED, so the step would re-ask forever. Set both or neither.
note2026_09_21_anthropic_assessment_prov.unchangedByDefault: ASSESSMENT_PROVIDER unset still selects deterministic, so nothing changes until the deployment is switched over. Pinned by a test.
note2026_09_21_anthropic_assessment_prov.stillOpen: DeterministicAssessmentModel remains an English stop list and is still the fallback whenever the provider fails. It would accept "네 있었어요" again. Hardening it was the other half of the recommendation and has not been done.

note2026_09_21_s02_ask_for_the_moment.task: The walkthrough asked a yes/no question and stored the answer as a list item. Reworded to ask for the moment itself.
note2026_09_21_s02_ask_for_the_moment.why: "최근에 이런 생각을 하신 적이 있으신가요? 떠오르지 않으면 없다고 말씀해 주셔도 괜찮아요" invites "네 있었어요" -- and the way-out sentence at the end hands them the mirror of itself. The shape of the question and what the answer gets stored as did not match. The model-judged gate (note2026_09_21_s02_model_judges_the_answer) handles it when it happens; this removes a cause.
note2026_09_21_s02_ask_for_the_moment.fourPlaces: The wording lives in four places and all four had the closed form: the composed fallback in s02/messages.ts (what a participant actually sees), walkthroughAskIntent's obtain in s02/task-intents.ts, the last-resort patientText in s02/spec.ts, and the step-specific clarification for "무슨 질문이요?" in runtime-execution-api.ts. Leaving the last one closed would have handed the yes/no straight back in the explanation.
note2026_09_21_s02_ask_for_the_moment.sharedFileJustification: runtime-execution-api.ts:213-215 is a shared file but an S02-only string, gated on the hardcoded prompt id tbct-s02-n05-p01-review-distortion, in the block already retargeted to the walkthrough in stage 1. Strings only; no logic touched.
note2026_09_21_s02_ask_for_the_moment.wayOutKept: "떠오르지 않으면 그렇게 말씀해 주셔도 괜찮아요" rather than "없다고 말씀해 주세요". Having no example is a real answer and hasNoExampleForPattern reads that reply to record an empty row, and 떠오르지 않 is already in NO_EXAMPLE_CONTAINS -- so the escape still parses while inviting the yes/no less.
note2026_09_21_s02_ask_for_the_moment.alsoAGeneralRule: walkthroughAskIntent's keep gained "Ask for the moment itself, not for a yes or no" with the reason, so the shape does not drift back on a rephrase.
note2026_09_21_s02_ask_for_the_moment.verificationLimit: Whether this actually reduces "네 있었어요" shows only in a live session; the offline assessment accepts most sentences. What the tests pin is that the question no longer asks a yes/no in either locale, that the way out survives, and that the clarification path does not re-ask one.
note2026_09_21_s02_ask_for_the_moment.s01NotInScope: S01's three list questions are closed in Korean too ("또 다른 어려움이 있을까요? 없으면 없다고 하셔도 괜찮아요") and it has no model-judged gate at all, so its exposure is larger. Deliberately left until S02 has been run live -- the same structure should not be spread to two sessions before it is confirmed in one.

note2026_09_21_s02_model_judges_the_answ.task: "네 있었어요" was filed in the worksheet as the participant's example for pattern 3, while the guide was -- correctly -- asking them what the example actually was. The real example, given on the next turn, was never stored.
note2026_09_21_s02_model_judges_the_answ.cause: Mine. The shared collection path already asks the model whether an answer IS an item before storing anything (runtime-input-assessment.ts's S02_COLLECTION_FIELDS -> runtime-context.ts's turnAction dispatch: accept_answer appends their wording verbatim, clarification_request/unresolved store nothing and leave the field missing so the step asks again). distortionExamples has been in that set since stage 1. Building the two-turn discussion, I moved the prompt's outputFields to the scratch scalar distortionTurnAnswer -- which took the step OFF that path, and a keyword list in s02/turn-rules.ts (isAcknowledgementOnly, looksLikeDistortionUnclear) became the thing deciding what counted as an example.
note2026_09_21_s02_model_judges_the_answ.fix: outputFields back to distortionExamples with validation.kind array, so the model decides again. turn-rules keeps only the STEP: which pattern the loop is on, ask vs discuss, the empty-row case, and when the walkthrough is done. looksLikeDistortionUnclear deleted; isAcknowledgementOnly kept for the discussion turn's own ending rule, not for judging an answer.
note2026_09_21_s02_model_judges_the_answ.rowAccounting: By the time turn rules run, the collection path has already appended, so there is no 'before' left to compare against. s02RowCount holds how many rows the walkthrough has settled; an ask turn that accepted shows rows.length > s02RowCount, a discussion turn trims back to it, and the empty-row case rebuilds from it. Without this the phase never advanced, because fields was compared against itself.
note2026_09_21_s02_model_judges_the_answ.whatTheTestsCanShow: The offline deterministic assessment accepts most sentences, so it cannot demonstrate the reported bug. The contract is pinned instead with a scripted assessment model (setAssessmentModelForTests, the idiom the untracked collection-semantic-gate.test.ts uses): clarification_request stores nothing, keeps the pattern and does not start the discussion; accept_answer files it and moves to the discussion. The old test that asserted the keyword behaviour was removed rather than adjusted -- it pinned the thing that was wrong.
note2026_09_21_s02_model_judges_the_answ.fixtureKey: session-fidelity-fixtures.ts pool key back to /distortionExamples/i. Left on the scratch name it matched nothing, the generic three-sentence fallback cycled, isDuplicateListEntry rejected the repeats and S02 audited at 67 turns with 15 fallbacks.

note2026_09_21_cdquest_grid_always_and_e.task: Three follow-ups on the grid: show it from the start, let the participant correct a score the way they can correct an example, and explain how to read it once instead of fifteen times.
note2026_09_21_cdquest_grid_always_and_e.alwaysVisible: First shipped gated to the scoring steps, reasoning that the recording brings the grid out at 43:00. That was wrong about the instrument: the participant's own copy (CD Quest Client version 1) is ONE sheet carrying the matrix ('1 2 3 / 2 3 4 / 3 4 5') beside the fifteen 'enter a personal example of...' fields. The form shows both the whole time, so the worksheet does too.
note2026_09_21_cdquest_grid_always_and_e.editableScore: The guide reads the score out of what the participant SAYS, so a misread one is a measured value that would otherwise stay wrong -- and the example cell beside it has always been editable. Clicking the chip opens the same frequency/intensity buttons the homework form uses (GradeButtons, now exported from cdquest-form.tsx), and saving writes cdQuestScores, cdQuestFrequency and cdQuestIntensity together so a row never holds a score apart from what it was made of.
note2026_09_21_cdquest_grid_always_and_e.totalFollowsTheRows: Session Signals sums the scores on screen rather than reading cdQuestTotal, so a corrected score shows at once. The two agree unless a row was edited after the program worked the total out; cdQuestTotal is only what the total step speaks, and the homework baseline already computed from cdQuestScores rather than from it.
note2026_09_21_cdquest_grid_always_and_e.explainOnce: scoringIntent branches on whether anything has been scored yet. First pattern: read one cell out loud as a worked example ('six or seven days and only a little comes to a 3'), then ask. After that: ask straight out, no walkthrough -- unless they ask how it works, which is explicitly still allowed. Reciting the bands fifteen times is what made the scoring read as a form.

note2026_09_21_cdquest_grid_on_screen.task: There was no scoring grid anywhere in the session: the bands were recited in words, fifteen times over, and the worksheet only displayed the result. The grid is now beside the conversation and the turn points at it.
note2026_09_21_cdquest_grid_on_screen.fromTheRecording: The counselor put the form up and pointed at it -- '여기에는 빈도가 있고요 여기 밑에는 강도가 있습니다' (967-968), '요 매트릭스에 의해서' (985) -- and the participant then read her own score off it, answering '2점인 것 같아요' as often as she gave the two halves. readCdQuestAnswer already accepted a stated score; nothing had ever shown her the table it comes from.
note2026_09_21_cdquest_grid_on_screen.cellsAreComputed: CdQuestGrid renders cdQuestScore(frequency, intensity) per cell rather than a table typed into the component, so the grid a participant reads and the arithmetic the session records cannot drift apart. Pinned by a test that rebuilds the expected cells from the same function.
note2026_09_21_cdquest_grid_on_screen.whenItShows: From the step that explains it (cdQuestScalePresented / cdQuestScaleUnderstood) through the scoring, and whenever scores exist. Not during the walkthrough, where it would be one more thing to read while trying to think of an example -- the recording brought it out at 43:00 for the same reason.
note2026_09_21_cdquest_grid_on_screen.pointerRegressionFound: activeCanonicalFieldKey is the PROMPT's outputFields[0] (patient-session-page.tsx:473). Both loops now answer into a scratch scalar (distortionTurnAnswer, cdQuestItemScore) rather than the list they build, so the worksheet -- which matched only the list names -- had had NO current-row highlight since that change, and the scoring pointer had never once activated. Both now match the scratch name too, with a test.

note2026_09_21_ask_before_reading.task: The discussion turn read every example, however thin it was. It now collects the missing detail first when it cannot see where the pattern shows.
note2026_09_21_ask_before_reading.promptOnly: Two keep lines in walkthroughDiscussIntent, nothing else. The user asked for the prompt first and no code. This is an instruction, not a guarantee -- the same layer that already failed once, when the catastrophizing turn dropped half its definition despite that definition being in the prompt.
note2026_09_21_ask_before_reading.whyThePromptIsTheRightLayerHere: Whether an example is thin enough to need a question is the judgement the model exists for. Code could only approximate it by length, which is what addsSomethingNew already does and is the weakest part of that design. The choice is 'instruct it' or 'do not do it', not 'code it precisely'.
note2026_09_21_ask_before_reading.notExplorationOnPurpose: conversationMove: explore would be the obvious mechanism and is wrong here. MAX_EXPLORATION_TURNS_PER_SESSION is 6, counted over the whole session (recentMessages is view.messages, not a window), and the walkthrough alone has fifteen patterns. It would work six times and then REJECT the turn (exploration_not_held) and ship the approved text, which is worse than never doing it. The discussion turn already asks and waits, so the question is simply the turn's own question, conversationMove advance, no budget involved and no shared file touched. Note explorationTurnsInStep is hardcoded to 0 in runtime-orchestrator.ts, so the per-step cap never binds.
note2026_09_21_ask_before_reading.knownGap: s02/turn-rules.ts decides how long a discussion runs from the length of the reply, so a question the guide asks can be answered and then cut off as the loop moves to the next pattern. The fix discussed was to hold one more turn when the previous discussion turn ended in a question; deferred at the user's request until the prompt alone is seen in a live session.
note2026_09_21_ask_before_reading.verificationLimit: Offline this can only be pinned as 'the instruction reaches the contract'. Whether it is followed shows only in a live session.

note2026_09_21_distortion_definitions_au.task: All fifteen registry definitions checked line by line against the recorded second session, after the catastrophizing turn came out missing its point.
note2026_09_21_distortion_definitions_au.result: Nine matched. One real omission and four partial ones, all amended. The rest of the audit is recorded here so it does not have to be redone.
note2026_09_21_distortion_definitions_au.mindReadingWasWrong: The counselor states it in BOTH directions -- '내가 남의 마음을 읽을 수 있다고 보고 남도 내 마음을 읽을 수 있다고 보는 거죠' (536-538) -- and the third example he gives runs the other way. The entry had one direction only. Second example added.
note2026_09_21_distortion_definitions_au.partial: emotional-reasoning: the counselor frames the feeling as the EVIDENCE (221) and his first example is a POSITIVE one, so the entry now says 증거 and carries both directions. selective-abstraction: '그래서 전체적인 결과를 내가 인정하지 못하는 결과가 생기게 되겠죠' (480-482). personalizing: fifteen lines on why the cashier is not smiling, ending '그 상황을 보는 게 아니라 유독 나한테만' (618-637) -- the unweighed situational reasons are what make it a distortion. what-if: '지금은 아픈 게 없어요, 차사고도 나지 않았고' (838-840) -- it is about what has NOT happened.
note2026_09_21_distortion_definitions_au.matchedAlready: dichotomous-thinking, fortune-telling-catastrophizing (the definition already carried 견딜 수 없을 정도로), discounting-positive, labeling, magnification-minimization, overgeneralization, should-statements, jumping-to-conclusions, blaming, unfair-comparisons.
note2026_09_21_distortion_definitions_au.theRealFailureWasDelivery: The reported defect was NOT a wrong definition: catastrophizing already said the outcome is taken as unbearable, and the guide dropped that half while paraphrasing. Nothing required it to survive -- the walkthrough's only mustMention is the pattern NAME. Addressed with a keep line rather than a per-pattern gate, since the user rejected gating the wording: several of the fifteen are defined in two parts and half of one is a different pattern.
note2026_09_21_distortion_definitions_au.sharedFileNote: cognitive-distortions.ts is shared with S01, whose candidate text composes descriptionKo verbatim. The amended definitions therefore also improve S01's suggestions, which is intended. S01's tests assert non-emptiness and compose from the registry, so no S01 text is pinned. descriptionEn kept short on purpose: distortion-candidates.ts composes up to five of them into one message against a 700-character cap.
note2026_09_21_distortion_definitions_au.notDone: The consequence the counselor attaches to should-statements (anger) is not in the entry. Left out because it is a consequence rather than what the pattern IS, and the other fourteen entries do not carry consequences either.

note2026_09_21_structured_output_leak.task: A turn reached the participant ending '...어떻게 느껴지세요?</patientFacingMessage>\n<parameter name="keepCurrentNode">true'. The model wrote the rest of its structured call inside the first field and nothing between there and the screen looked at the text.
note2026_09_21_structured_output_leak.sharedFileJustification: dialogue-output-validator.ts is the only place the patient-facing text is inspected before it ships, and the defect is session-agnostic -- any of the eight can produce it. It cannot be caught session-locally. One guard added (structured_output_leak, enforce) and one pattern; no existing guard changed.
note2026_09_21_structured_output_leak.whyEnforceNotLog: The other content guards are log-mode because their matches are judgement calls. This one is not: a patient must never read markup, and the approved text is always a better turn than a broken one. Enforcing also means one rewrite is tried first.
note2026_09_21_structured_output_leak.tests: dialogue-agent.test.ts: four leaked shapes rejected with reason structured_output_leak, three ordinary sentences (including one with quoted speech) unaffected, and the guard mode pinned.
note2026_09_21_structured_output_leak.notDiagnosed: Why the model produced it. The Anthropic path uses a proper tool_use block and guards stop_reason=max_tokens, so the malformed output came back inside the tool input itself. Worth watching in the turn records if it recurs.

note2026_09_21_worksheet_text_fused_form.task: The cell still held '...좋았던거라고 생각했음' after the first cleanup pass.
note2026_09_21_worksheet_text_fused_form.cause: That pass only removed a DETACHED quote ('...싫어할꺼야 라고 생각했습니다') and deliberately left the fused form alone, because cutting at the particle leaves '...좋았던거'. Leaving it alone was safe but did not do the job.
note2026_09_21_worksheet_text_fused_form.fix: Three shapes now, each leaving grammatical Korean: a detached quote loses the frame; '거/것 + 라고 + report verb' unwinds to '거야'; '-다고 + report verb' unwinds to '-다'; and a nominalised report ('...어떡하지 하는 생각이 들어요') loses the tail. Anything else still falls through to the sentence-end check and is left as written.
note2026_09_21_worksheet_text_fused_form.honestCaveat: The 거야 branch adds a syllable the participant did not type. It is the plain form their own quotative was quoting, not new content, and it is the only way to leave that shape grammatical -- but it is an addition, not purely a removal.

note2026_09_21_s02_one_step_per_message.task: Two defects visible in the first live S02 run, once the dialogue agent was actually reached.
note2026_09_21_s02_one_step_per_message.duplication: The rationale node said the same thing twice in a row: the research message ended with what the pattern list gets used for later, and the next message repeated it. Cause: the contract's therapeuticObjective is the NODE's objective (dialogue-contract-compiler.ts:441) and every prompt in the node receives it, so an objective that reads 'say three things' invites each turn to say all three. Five S02 nodes carry more than one prompt and all had the same exposure. Fixed with a session rule (each message covers only its own step) plus a keep line on research-evidence.
note2026_09_21_s02_one_step_per_message.falseAcknowledgement: A message the program does not wait on opened with '네, 좋아요', agreeing with something said two messages earlier. lastParticipantMessage stays set across consecutive program messages, so the rule is keyed on whether the turn waits for an answer instead.
note2026_09_21_s02_one_step_per_message.worksheetText: The cell held the whole sentence, reporting frame and all: '...나를 싫어할꺼야 라고 생각했습니다'. normalizeExampleForWorksheet takes the frame off, deterministically -- no model, no summarising, nothing reworded, because distortionExamples is assistantMustNotSupply and the ask was to clean rather than summarise. The chat message keeps what they typed.
note2026_09_21_s02_one_step_per_message.worksheetTextIsNarrowOnPurpose: Korean fuses the quotative particle into the clause as often as it detaches it. Cutting at the particle in '...무너질 거라고 생각했어요' leaves '...무너질 거', and the first build of this did exactly that to five of eleven test sentences. So the frame comes off ONLY when what remains already ends like a finished sentence; the fused case is left exactly as written. A miss costs nothing, a bad cut would. Reconstructing the fused case would mean adding words the participant did not write.

note2026_09_21_s02_walkthrough_discussio.task: The fifteen-pattern walkthrough collected an example per pattern and moved straight on. The real session spent two thirds of its time TALKING about those examples. Each pattern now takes two turns: ask, then discuss what they said.
note2026_09_21_s02_walkthrough_discussio.userDecision: Asked for what the recording's counselor actually does -- pointing at part of the participant's own sentence and saying that part is this pattern, and suggesting a better-fitting example of their own. Explicitly did not want the wording forced by code.
note2026_09_21_s02_walkthrough_discussio.evidence: ~/Desktop/석사/연구실/TBCT/공동연구/상담/2회기/TBCT_2회기_전사_20260918.txt. The counselor's move is the same three beats on nearly every pattern: quote their words back, name the move, name the pattern. Lines 561-575 (mind reading), 384-393 (labeling), 578-600 (a six-turn Socratic build for overgeneralization), 305-330 (a replacement example for the SAME pattern, not a re-filing).
note2026_09_21_s02_walkthrough_discussio.classificationScope: The loop names the pattern, so the guide confirms ONE named pattern and never chooses among fifteen. It may say other patterns show through too (the counselor's own answer to the difficulty reported in the homework review). It may NOT rank the fifteen, choose on the participant's behalf, or move a row. Changing WHICH of the participant's examples fills a row is allowed -- the counselor did that once -- because the label never moves.
note2026_09_21_s02_walkthrough_discussio.researchBasis: The shape is published as Diagnosis-of-Thought prompting (Chen et al., EMNLP 2023 Findings): separate fact from thought, contrast the reasoning, then name it; its rationales were approved by expert raters. Its documented failure is over-diagnosis -- asked to find the pattern, a model finds one even when there is none -- which ERD (arXiv 2403.14255) improved by extracting the span first. Hence the explicit way out in the discuss intent. Two limits on how hard it may push come from an evaluation of an LLM cognitive-restructuring chatbot (ACM Trans. Computing for Healthcare / arXiv 2501.15599): participants read 'a classic example' as being judged, and insisting on a reading rather than offering it once felt invalidating. note2026_09_21_s01_closing_recap.task: S01 ends at homework -> homework consent -> goodbye, with no recap of what the session covered. The book this protocol comes from (de Oliveira, Trial-Based Cognitive Therapy, ch.1, 'Designing Homework, Summarizing, and Concluding Session 1') and the real first session S01 follows (GMT20260911 recording, 62:50-63:23, right after 'can you do that' / 'I think I can') both have the therapist recap the session between the homework and the goodbye.
note2026_09_21_s01_closing_recap.userDecision: 2026-09-21, by the user: the COUNSELOR gives the recap, as in the real session, and it covers the whole session. It goes in the last node. The wording is Claude's (task intent), not a fixed sentence -- step order, completion and safety stay in code, the wording does not. The feedback request that follows the recap in the book and the recording is deliberately LEFT OUT: taking feedback means carrying it into the next session, which is separate work for later.
note2026_09_21_s01_closing_recap.keyObservation: The recap in the real recording names none of the participant's own content -- not the difficulty, not the goal, not the situation. It is entirely a recap of what was DONE ('we looked at the difficulties you have, we set a goal, we understood the cognitive model through your case and through three people's cases, ... we looked at those fifteen patterns'). So the step is a process recap, not a read-back of their answers, which is why the wording can be left to Claude: there is almost nothing to get wrong, and 'name none of their answers' is a rule rather than a template.
note2026_09_21_s01_closing_recap.noConfirmationQuestion: By the user, after weighing it: the recap does not ask 'is that right'. It is in neither the book nor the recording; the participant's own understanding was already taken at n16 participant-summary, and asking twice weakens that step; and a 'no' would have no clinical script at the very end of the session. The step asks nothing and the session closes on the goodbye that follows.
note2026_09_21_s01_closing_recap.notStored: The recap text is not written to any field. Claude phrases it differently each time, so the S07/S08 pattern (compose the string, then record the identical string in applyPromptCompletionEffect) does not apply, and capturing the delivered assistant message would need a new shared-runtime path -- out of proportion here. The recap is in the conversation log, which is what the clinician reads. Revisit together with the feedback step.
